assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the two reviewed items curated on tomozaki:michael-andi@light-novel at basis_commit, each read in full: #bounded-character-dossier, the canonical B-scope Michael Andi bounded posthumous character dossier (INDEPENDENT_BOUNDED_LITERARY_SCOPE_PASS, scope B_posthumous_artifact_and_testimony_bounded), whose positive person evidence is Japanese V12 surviving documents and attributed island testimony (MA-E01 to MA-E09, MA-P01 to MA-P08), with earlier volumes routed only as Kikuchi's and Fumiya's reception (MA-P09); and #attributed-retrieval-model, the canonical derived-use attributed retrieval/constraint model (MA1 to MA6), marked do_not_use_as_primary_literary_authority, which derives from the dossier, enacts no current or posthumous interior and is not used as literary evidence. The project's current-state entrypoint was read for method and gate state only. The supporting character implementation review, the supporting literary evidence manifest, the historical and context retrieval integration review, operator guide and packet, the accepted Kikuchi study and the ledgers (CRI section 18, CS section 19.1, REL section 17.1) are not curated on this subject and are not evidence here. No published Andi novel text, adaptation, performed voice or post-V12 material is in scope.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Andi's historical island presence as attributed after his death in V12: more than ten years of reported visits ending in a last year of desk work, with the order of the fish, prank, drinking, cloth and story-night reports not established; the V12 inquiry state is a record held by others (tower, cloths, private continuation), not a living Andi state. Earlier-volume material is later readers' reception, not his biography. Age, dates and mechanism of death and publication chronology are unknown.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The dossier records reported wants (continued work, returning to the island, tasting and recovering different responses, describing a changing sea, reading continuations to listeners) and states that their hierarchy is unknown (section 9); every motive explanation is attributed to a teller: the fish worker's dislike-of-understanding guess (MA-E03) and the couple's godlike-observer and remaining-self/prayer reconstructions (MA-E07, section 8). The model retrieves these with their tellers and refuses to resolve gaps in his voice. D is rejected because no mechanism of his is represented in conduct, only proposed by others, and the row itself disclaims psychology. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the reported wants and the attribution of every hypothesis are located.

The fish account has internal stages in its telling (cannot swallow, returns, likes, interviews, recovers dislike; MA-P04), and the innkeeper reports visits over more than ten years with long desk hours in the last year (MA-P03). The dossier warns that these accounts may have different clocks and refuses to make them one continuous biography (section 4), and V12's change is in Kikuchi's received image, not in the dead man (section 3; model MA1). D is rejected because no development of his is dated or witnessed and the reports are not ordered; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the reported stages and the explicit chronology limits are located.

The discovery row does not claim SPEECH. Located words are a few reported quotations (the breakfast-fish claim, the drunken statement that he had written only observation records, the wish to recover dislike) and the English verbs of the private continuation read through phone translation (MA-P02 to MA-P04, MA-P07). The dossier rejects retrotranslating any original sentence and rejects new wise answers in his voice; the model awards no new dialogue, idiolect or acoustics. D is rejected because no register features are described; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the quotations and their mediated status are located.

Ordinary conduct is reported by several distinct witnesses: repeated stays and a breakfast-fish ritual (innkeeper, MA-P03), writing while watching the coast (shopwoman, MA-P02), drinking (liquor seller), repeated taste experiments and interviews (fish workers, MA-P04), bringing shop cloth to compare with the sea and fixing the telescope (Mitsu, MA-P05), plus present material traces. C is rejected because every item is retrospective testimony with admitted gaps and possibly different eras, and no ordinary scene of his is represented. E is rejected because the routine is distributed across independent tellers and material traces rather than one local episode.

The dossier's section 9 table separates the innkeeper, fish workers, the shopkeeper and translation helper, the liquor seller, Mitsu, historical listeners and later readers, each with its access, support and exclusions; the model requires returning the teller and evidence kind with each claim. Mitsu's craft exchange, nuisance and custodial labor and the translation helper's anger at his prank are recipient-specific. C is rejected because each relation reaches the reader only through one teller's recollection, no exchange is shown, and Mitsu's standing and the unnamed women's identities remain open. E is rejected because recipient-differentiated reports and limits are explicitly tabulated.

No interior of Andi's is rendered: the dossier names his authentic interior and intentions OPEN (section 12), the manuscript marks show selection without reasons (MA-E06), and the inward accounts offered are the couple's hypotheses (MA-E07). D is rejected because nothing beyond reported self-statements and attributed guesses exists; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence affirmatively characterizes what is and is not accessible.

Friction is reported, not shown: the translation helper throws an ashtray after his crab prank and he runs (MA-P02); fish workers call his repeated questioning troublesome (MA-P04); Mitsu complains of the fixed telescope (MA-P05). D is rejected because these are a few remembered anecdotes with no represented confrontation of his; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the reported frictions are located.

No ethical deliberation of Andi's own is located, and the discovery row disclaims ethics and decision-making. The dossier's ethical material concerns later readers' use of his papers and the limits of the circled verb (sections 8 and 10), which bounds the scenario below but does not evidence his own weighing. Nothing is established either way about how he deliberated.

The crab prank, his laughter and the reversal when the helper retaliates (MA-P02), and the excitement the fish workers recall at each change of taste (MA-P04), are reported mischief and delight; the dossier refuses to read them as harmless charm or a license. D is rejected because play rests on one prank anecdote and remembered enthusiasm; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the reported acts are located.

An independently reviewed B-scope posthumous dossier with exact V12 member and paragraph windows (MA-P01 to MA-P08) and an inherited reception route (MA-P09), paired with an accepted attributed retrieval model. C is rejected because the person evidence is one volume of attributed testimony and one translation-mediated document, the dossier claims no complete new V12 primary reread, and the reviews, manifest, packet, Kikuchi study and ledgers are not curated on this subject. E is rejected because the dossier is independently reviewed with exact located windows.

Both items state affirmative located limits: the innkeeper does not know whether the last manuscript was completed (MA-P03); the liquor seller says she cannot explain his statement and heard it as drunk talk (MA-P02), and his published novels counter a literal reading of it; the dislike-of-understanding motive is a resident's hypothesis (MA-P04); the unnamed women are not identified with each other or Mitsu and no romance follows (MA-P02, MA-P05); record is itself crossed out before pray, defeating a pure-transcription account (MA-E06/E07); twelve rival readings are disposed (section 11). B is rejected because the limits rest on a few V12 testimony windows and several are stated unknowns rather than contradictions shown across contexts; D is rejected because these are located, subject-specific limits.

The dossier requires selecting one of four access bands (earlier reception, historical island presence, V12 inquiry, unshown future) before any claim and binds each to exact windows; the model repeats the selector requirement (MA1). C is rejected because within the historical band the order and dates of the reports are explicitly unestablished and his age and death date are unknown, so dated knowledge states cannot be reconstructed. E is rejected because claims are bound to distinct located bands with explicit knowledge exclusions.

scenario_readiness.note: The model supplies no new first-person voice, no new Japanese dialogue and no idiolect, and the dossier rejects a posthumous dossier generating new wise answers in Andi's voice (section 11). CONDITIONAL would invent a voice from a few reported quotations; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly bounds voice.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The historical island band only, as attributed after his death in V12, with report order unestablished; earlier volumes are reception and the V12 inquiry is a record held by others, not a living Andi state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Only attested recipients in their reported standing: the innkeeper, fish workers, the shopkeeper and translation helper, the liquor seller, Mitsu as craft partner and custodian, and island listeners; later readers never meet him.
setting_constraints: The island inn, harbor, shops, tower and story nights as reported only
No new manuscript content, final testament, motive declaration, romance or endorsement of later readers
Output would be attributed retrieval with labeled tellers and alternatives, never an enacted persona or new dialogue

scenario_readiness.note: The model is manual attributed retrieval that returns tellers, evidence kinds and abstentions and never takes up the dead author's voice; the dossier's comparison domains are explicitly not scenario outputs or a reconstruction model (section 12). CONDITIONAL would enact a person known only through others' recollections; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly bounds transfer.

Ordinary social conduct is retrievable from distributed reports (rituals, questioning, pranks, drinking), but the model enacts no persona and the dossier keeps every act attributed to its teller. CONDITIONAL would generate ordinary behavior from testimony with possibly different eras; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the reports and their limits are located.

The dossier and model reject treating the circled pray as a testament or general permission and reject new ethical answers in his voice (sections 10 to 11; MA5, MA6); no deliberation of his own is rendered. CONDITIONAL would invent the weighing the record withholds; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly bounds the scenario.

The evidence affirmatively blocks romance: the unnamed women are not identified, the prank establishes no reciprocity, and Mitsu's intimacy and custody do not make her wife or lover (sections 2, 4, 5 and 11; MA3). CONDITIONAL would supply a relationship the dossier rejects; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly bounds it.

His work as an author is the best-evidenced domain (long desk hours, observation labor, cloth arrays, the believe-tell-record-wish-pray revision), but it is known only through testimony, material traces and one translation-mediated document, and the model retrieves it without enacting decisions. CONDITIONAL would generate new authorial choices or manuscript content the dossier forbids; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the work practice and its limits are located.

known_limits.statement: His authentic interior, intentions and motive hierarchy are OPEN (dossier sections 9 and 12); the fish-motive explanation is a resident's hypothesis (MA-P04) and the godlike-observer and remaining-self/prayer accounts are Kikuchi's and Fumiya's reconstructions (MA-E07).
Whether マイケル・アンディ is a legal or pen name, his nationality, age, family, education, dates and mechanism of death and publication chronology are unknown at this scope (MA-P01).
The innkeeper does not know whether the last manuscript was completed (MA-P03), and the liquor seller cannot explain his observation-records statement and heard it as drunk talk (MA-P02).

On the private continuation believe, tell, record and wish are crossed out and pray is circled (V12 p0021 P267-329); the marks establish revision and selection on those pages, not reasons, a final doctrine, a last thought or permission for later uses.
The shopwoman's unnamed woman and the translation helper are not identified with each other or with Mitsu, and no wife, lover or romance is established (MA-P02, MA-P05).
Earlier-volume Andi material is Kikuchi's and Fumiya's reception and does not show Andi's knowledge of those readers or a present development in him (MA-E01, MA-P09).
No scene of Andi alive is represented; all conduct reaches the reader as recollection, material trace or translated document after his death.
The dossier claims no complete new V12 primary reread, and the implementation and integration reviews, manifest, packet, operator guide, Kikuchi study and ledgers are not curated on this subject.
No idiolect, habitual distribution or acoustic manner is established, his published prose is not in evidence, and generated speech was not evaluated.
